correctness.rationale: At area elasticity alpha=3/4, Holder gives the exact variational identity max_a rho(W(a)) = max_{z>=0, sum z_i^(8/7)=1} 2 sum_{edges P4} z_i z_j. The converse uses a_i=z_i^(8/7), x_i=z_i^(4/7). Since p=8/7>1 and graph connected, a zero coordinate in a maximizing z can be perturbed by epsilon with objective gain O(epsilon) exceeding O(epsilon^p) renormalization loss; hence a positive global maximizer exists. Reflection-symmetric points reduce to F(t)=2^(-3/4)(1+2t^7)/(1+t^8)^(7/4) with unique maximum t0+t0^8=1. Direct rational checks bound 8116/10000 < t0 < 8117/10000 and F(t0)<161/250. For explicit positive r=(5,10,11,10), S=sum r_i^8=414749506, Q=2 sum (r_i r_(i+1))^7=781049340000000, an independent exact-integer comparison gives Q^4>(161/250)^4 S^7, proving asymmetric rho>161/250. Symmetry then forces every actual global optimum to be asymmetric and reflected in distinct pairs. For path P2, AM-GM gives the unique equal split; for P3, strict concavity of exponent 3/4 and a2(1-a2) uniquely optimize a1=a3 and a2=1/2, so P4 is minimal among paths. These assert only the linear mean-field invasion threshold tau_c=1/rho, not stochastic survival, unique P4 optimizer or other elasticities.
